references.text: The angels warn Lot about the coming destruction of Sodom and instruct him to gather his family, which leads directly to Lot going out to warn his sons-in-law.
After Lot's failed attempt to persuade his sons-in-law, the angels urge Lot and his immediate family to leave the city before its destruction.
Peter describes the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah and refers to Lot as righteous, shedding light on his efforts to save his family from judgment.
Jesus compares the last days to the days of Lot: people were eating, drinking, buying, and selling without taking the warning seriously—just as Lot's sons-in-law did not take him seriously.
Isaiah warns against mocking, lest the bonds be tightened—a thematic parallel to the sons-in-laws' scorn for Lot's warnings about God's judgment.
The people deny the Lord's judgment and regard the prophets' warnings as empty words, just as Lot's sons-in-law thought he was joking.
Parallel in prophetic role: A warning of judgment with a call to repentance, but with different reception (Lot is mocked, Jeremiah receives a response).
